A.J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Petitioner

Most. Shahida Khanam ------ Petitioner
Vs.
K.M. Zahurul Hoque and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 9. We have heard the submission of Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and also perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other materials on record. It appears that the High Court Division rightly found that exparte decree passed in favour of the defendant-respondent No.1 in Title Suit No.291 of 1985 was maintained up to the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No.361 of 2002. So he should not be deprived of enjoying the benefit of the said decree. The High Court Division is of the views that if the proceeding of the execution case in question is somehow blocked either in the form of injunction or stay the decree which the defendant-respondent No.1 obtained on 26.04.1989 shall be made nugatory and that will definitely shake the faith and confidence of the litigant people in judicial system of the country. The High Court Division is also of the view that if the plaintiff petitioner has filed the suit for declaration of her title and if she is evicted there from in execution of the decree there would be no bar to make necessary amendment in the plaint incorporating the said fact of eviction and making a prayer for recovery of khas possession thereof. It appears that the High Court Division has rightly noticed that the learned District Judge did not assign any reason whatsoever in passing the impugned order and he also failed to consider the fact that the plaintiff-petitioner admitted the filing of the previous suit by him challenging the exparte decree and dismissal of the suit by the Appellate Division. The High Court Division rightly found that the learned District Judge combined error of law on an important question of law that when the decree obtained by a party is maintained by the highest court of the country and such decree cannot   be made ineffective or nugatory somehow. Thus the learned Judges of the High Court Division rightly found that the learned District Judge committed error, of law in exercising its jurisdiction under Sub, Section (2) of Section 115 of the Code and in that view of the mater they have not considered it proper to send the respondent again to the Court of District Judge when Sub-Section (4) of the said Section gave the respondent the right to move the High Court Division. On perusal of the materials on record and the impugned judgment and order passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division and having considered the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute on proper consideration of the materials on record.
